goal: When the Solicitation lane finds no attribution for a suppression-bearing event, it writes the recipient's global Suppression ledger row from the signed provider payload and acks, so an account purge cannot destroy the global opt-out the purge contract preserves (#967).
non_goals: Finding the root cause of #965 — that ticket is re-triaged to an investigation, not fixed here.
Changing the Judge health probe (#949 stays tracked and unfixed).
Changing the notification lane, the unsubscribe ingress, or worker/ingress/resend.ts routing.
Changing #630's send lifecycle, the tx2 CAS, or when provider_message_id is persisted.
Adding a migration, a table, an env var, a feature flag, or a dependency.
Retroactively scrubbing or reprocessing inbound_events rows already sitting at status='failed'.
Widening the ws8-tier-wiring spec or the WS4 spec — only send-mode-executor-approval D9 gets the amendment.
user_visible_behavior: A permanent bounce, complaint, or email.suppressed event whose solicitation_outreach row no longer exists writes a scope='global' Suppression ledger row and returns 200, where it previously returned 503 and wrote nothing.
A recipient who bounced or complained after their sender's account was purged is never contacted again by any tenant.
checkFailedInboundEvents stops alerting for this class, because the event now lands status='processed'.
The stored raw payload for such an event now falls under ArchivalPoller's existing 30-day processed-event sweep instead of being retained forever as a failed row.
invariants: A global Suppression ledger row written after the purge boundary carries accountId: null (worker/jobs/account-offboarding/purge-stages.ts suppression contract).
recordSuppression stays the single chokepoint for every suppression write; the lane never inserts into solicitation_suppressions directly.
The ledger stays first-write-wins: repeated provider events for the same handle write at most one row.
The recipient address never reaches a log line.
normalizeEmail (src/lib/solicitation/handles.ts) stays the single owner of email normalization; the lane never re-spells it.
The lane's write surface stays narrow: no delivery_status, no sent_at, no unsubscribed_at, no delivered_at.
When attribution IS present, the provider-echoed recipient is ignored entirely — the existing rule survives, narrowed to that condition.
Soft bounces, email.failed, and email.delivery_delayed still never suppress.
edge_cases: data.to absent, not an array, or empty → throw (impossible state for a message this lane sent).
data.to carries two or more addresses → throw; a global row blocks that person for every tenant, so a wrong one is real harm.
data.to carries one address but normalizeEmail returns null (implausible syntax) → throw rather than mint an unmatchable key.
Attribution present → the payload recipient is never read; the contact row's stored handle wins.
Unmatched soft bounce or email.failed → unchanged warn-and-ack, no ledger write, no payload read.
Repeat event for an already-suppressed handle → recordSuppression no-ops and the lane still acks.

The seconds-wide race (send committed, provider_message_id not yet persisted) → the ledger row is written from the payload and the outreach bounced_at/complained_at stamp is NOT written. Accepted loss, owner-decided: the Send breaker undercounts one bounce, the compliance fact survives.
A CAS-lost send (dispatch.ts commitSendTerminal terminalized=0) never persists provider_message_id at all — the same fallback now covers that permanently-unattributable class too.

rollback_plan: Revert the commit. There is no schema change, no migration, and no feature flag, so the lane returns to throw-on-unmatched immediately. Global ledger rows already written stay: they are correct opt-outs and the ledger has no expiry by design.
observability: A Sentry warning `solicitation_suppression_without_attribution` from the fallback path, tagged feature/event/source and carrying event type and ledger source but never the recipient address. CORRECTED after the step-7 review: this was originally specified as a log line only, which was wrong — acking removes these events from checkFailedInboundEvents' status='failed' set, so the change retired a pager and a log nothing subscribes to does not replace one. A sustained rate means outreach rows are disappearing under live sends (the #965 class), so this alert is that open investigation's detector.

checkFailedInboundEvents (worker/background/pollers/health-alert/checks.ts) stops firing for resend suppression-bearing events — intended, and the reason the Sentry signal above is mandatory rather than nice-to-have. A continued alert means the fallback did not engage.
solicitation_suppressed analytics events (recordSuppression, §9.4) with scope='global' and a null account id are the durable proof the purge promise held.
